사다.x: I bought fruit at the market.
사다.e: Opposite of 팔다 (sell). 사 줄게 = 'I'll treat you' — common when buying a friend a meal.
사다.t: 사다 'buy' and 살다 'live' share forms like 사세요 — context tells them apart.

잠깐.forms: 잠깐 + verb: 잠깐 기다리세요 · 잠깐만요! (just a moment!)
잠깐.m: for a moment, briefly; a moment (noun)
잠깐.t: 잠깐만요! also works as 'Excuse me' to get past people in a crowd.

부터.forms: time + 부터 (아홉 시부터) · often 부터 … 까지
부터.e: Probably from 붙다 (to stick). Pairs with 까지: 9시부터 5시까지 = from 9 to 5.
부터.t: 부터 is mainly for time; for places use 에서: 서울에서 부산까지.

무료.ex: 이 박물관은 입장료가 하루 종일 무료예요.
무료.x: Admission to this museum is free all day.
무료.t: 무료 is the neutral word on signs and menus; 공짜 is the casual spoken word.

환불.x: You can't get a refund without a receipt.
환불.t: Customers say 환불을 받다 ("get a refund"); stores say 환불해 드릴게요 ("We'll refund you").

기대.x: I have high hopes for the new semester.
기대.e: Literally 'expect and wait' — waiting with hope.
기대.t: Don't confuse it with native 기대다 'to lean on': 벽에 기대요 = I lean against the wall.

칠판.x: The teacher wrote a problem on the board.

치즈.x: Please put more cheese on the pizza.
치즈.e: From English 'cheese', with an extra 으 vowel added at the end.
치즈.t: Koreans say '김치' or '치즈' when posing for photos, like 'say cheese'.

소년.ex: 한 소년이 공원에서 강아지와 놀고 있어요.
소년.x: A boy is playing with a puppy in the park.

절반.x: I split the pizza half and half with my friend.

그램.x: To make this cake, you need 200 grams of sugar.

넘어지다.m: to fall down, to trip, to fall over
넘어지다.x: The road was slippery, so I fell in front of the school.
넘어지다.e: 넘다 'go over' + -어지다: you go over and fall.

재다.x: I had my height and weight measured at the hospital today.

파도.ex: 오늘은 바람이 많이 불어서 파도가 높아요.
파도.x: It's very windy today, so the waves are high.
파도.e: Both syllables mean 'wave' — big rolling waves.
파도.t: Waves 'strike' in Korean: 파도가 치다 'waves break'.

사실.ex: 사실은 저도 그 영화를 아직 안 봤어요.
사실.x: Actually, I haven't seen that movie yet either.
사실.t: 사실은 at the start of a sentence means 'actually, to be honest'.

디자이너.x: My friend is a designer who makes clothes.

가전제품.x: When we moved, we bought all new appliances.

참여하다.m: to participate in, to take part in, to get involved
참여하다.ex: 많은 학생들이 환경 보호 캠페인에 참여했어요.
참여하다.x: Many students took part in the environmental protection campaign.
참여하다.e: Literally 'join and take part' plus 하다.
참여하다.t: Use the particle 에: 수업에 적극적으로 참여하세요 'Take an active part in class.'

소비.ex: 전기 소비를 줄이려면 불을 꼭 끄세요.
소비.x: To cut down on electricity use, be sure to turn off the lights.

판매하다.x: This store sells only organic vegetables.
판매하다.t: 판매하다 is the formal, business word; in daily talk just say 팔다.

보람.m: reward, worthwhileness (the feeling that effort paid off)
보람.x: I feel rewarded when I do volunteer work.
보람.e: Builds 보람 있다 and 보람차다, both meaning 'rewarding, worthwhile'.
보람.t: 보람 has no exact English match: it's the satisfying sense that your effort was worth it.

기준.x: Each company has different criteria for hiring employees.

초반.ex: 그는 이십 대 초반에 회사를 시작했어요.
초반.x: He started his company in his early twenties.
초반.e: Originally the opening stage of a board game such as baduk.
초반.t: Ages work like English: 20대 초반 is 'early twenties,' 30대 후반 is 'late thirties.'

은퇴하다.m: to retire (from work or a career)
은퇴하다.ex: 그 축구 선수는 서른다섯 살에 은퇴했어요.
은퇴하다.x: That soccer player retired at thirty-five.
은퇴하다.e: Literally 'withdraw out of sight' from public or working life.

고요하다.ex: 해가 뜨기 전 새벽의 바다는 아주 고요했어요.
고요하다.x: Before sunrise, the sea at dawn was very still.
고요하다.e: More poetic than 조용하다; often describes nature, nights, and atmospheres.

대체하다.ex: 많은 일을 이제 기계가 대체하고 있어요.
대체하다.x: Machines are now replacing a lot of jobs.

민감하다.x: My skin is very sensitive to sunlight.
민감하다.t: Pattern: N에 민감하다 (sensitive to N), used for skin, topics, and prices.

차트.x: The newly released song went to No. 1 on the chart.
차트.t: Also used for a patient's medical chart at a hospital.

키오스크.x: These days you order at a kiosk even in restaurants.
키오스크.e: From English 'kiosk'; in Korea it almost always means a touchscreen machine for ordering and paying, not a street stall.
키오스크.t: Common in fast-food places and cafés. Many older people find them hard to use, so some shops keep a staffed counter too.

기관.ex: 정부 기관에서 일하려면 시험을 봐야 해요.
기관.x: To work at a government agency, you have to take an exam.
기관.e: Originally 'mechanism'; now the working bodies that keep society running.
기관.t: 기관 is for official bodies: 정부 기관, 교육 기관, 의료 기관.

검찰.ex: 검찰은 그 사건을 다시 조사하기로 했습니다.
검찰.x: The prosecution decided to investigate the case again.

감정적.ex: 화가 나도 감정적으로 말하지 않으려고 노력해요.
감정적.x: Even when I'm angry, I try not to speak emotionally.
감정적.e: -적 turns a noun into '-al/-ic': 감정적, 경제적, 문화적.
감정적.t: Use 감정적인 before nouns and 감정적으로 as an adverb; 감정적이다 works as a predicate.

태연하다.x: Even after lying, he kept a straight face.
태연하다.t: Often slightly negative: acting calm when you shouldn't be, as in 태연하게 거짓말하다.

과감하다.x: The company boldly invested in a new market.

어쨌거나.m: anyway, in any case, whatever the case
어쨌거나.x: Anyway, I'm really glad the exam is over.
어쨌거나.e: Contraction of 어찌했거나, 'however it was done'.
어쨌거나.t: Pronounced [어짿꺼나]; casual, and 어쨌든 is the everyday equivalent.

제기하다.m: to raise (a question, issue), to file (a lawsuit)
제기하다.ex: 한 기자가 정부 발표에 의문을 제기했어요.
제기하다.x: A reporter raised questions about the government's announcement.
제기하다.t: Fixed collocations: 문제를 제기하다, 의문을 제기하다, 소송을 제기하다.

실용적.x: This bag looks nice and is practical too.

진땀을 빼다.forms: 진땀을 빼요 · 진땀을 뺐어요 · 진땀(을) 흘리다
진땀을 빼다.m: to sweat bullets, to have a really hard time
진땀을 빼다.ex: 갑자기 질문을 받아서 대답하느라 진땀을 뺐어요.
진땀을 빼다.x: I got a surprise question and sweated bullets trying to answer.
진땀을 빼다.e: 진땀 = sticky sweat from stress or strain; literally 'to squeeze out sticky sweat.'

팬덤.ex: 그 그룹의 팬덤은 전 세계에 있어요.
팬덤.x: That group has a fandom all over the world.
팬덤.t: Most K-pop groups have an official name for their fandom.

꼰대.m: condescending know-it-all; preachy older person or boss (slang)
꼰대.ex: 우리 부장님은 좋은 분인데 가끔 꼰대 같아요.
꼰대.x: My department head is a good person, but sometimes acts like a preachy know-it-all.
꼰대.e: Old slang for one's father or teacher; its origin is uncertain. Now it means anyone who lectures others and insists 'my way is right'.
꼰대.t: Casual and critical — never say it to someone's face. The joke phrase 라떼는 말이야 (a pun on 나 때는 말이야 'back in my day') mocks typical 꼰대 talk. Young people can be 꼰대 too (젊은 꼰대).

제휴.ex: 두 회사는 기술 개발을 위해 제휴를 맺었습니다.
제휴.x: The two companies formed a partnership for technology development.
제휴.t: Collocation: 제휴를 맺다 = to form a partnership; 제휴 카드 is a co-branded card.

조례.x: The city council passed a new environmental ordinance.
조례.e: Literally 'rules in articles'; a homonym 조례 means a school morning assembly.

천체.x: On the weekend, I observed celestial bodies at the observatory with a friend.

이의를 제기하다.forms: N에 이의를 제기하다 · 이의를 제기했어요 · 이의 있습니다! (formal objection)
이의를 제기하다.m: to raise an objection, to object, to challenge
이의를 제기하다.ex: 몇몇 회원들이 회의 결과에 이의를 제기했습니다.
이의를 제기하다.x: Several members raised objections to the outcome of the meeting.
이의를 제기하다.t: In meetings, 이의 있습니까? asks 'Any objections?' — answer 이의 없습니다.

연계하다.m: to link, to connect, to coordinate with
연계하다.ex: 학교는 지역 기업과 연계해 취업 프로그램을 운영해요.
연계하다.x: The school runs a job program in partnership with local companies.

간추리다.m: to summarize, to condense, to sort out the essentials
간추리다.x: I summarized the meeting and reported it to the team leader.
간추리다.e: Related to 추리다 'to pick out' — selecting only the key points.

더러.ex: 이 동네에서도 더러 외국인을 볼 수 있어요.
더러.x: You can occasionally see foreigners in this neighborhood, too.
더러.e: Homonym warning: unrelated to 더럽다 'dirty' and to the particle 더러 'to (someone)'.

실로.ex: 우리가 다시 만난 건 실로 십 년 만이에요.
실로.x: It's truly been ten years since we last met.
실로.t: More formal than 정말; often heard in speeches, e.g. 실로 감격스럽습니다.

손에 땀을 쥐다.forms: 손에 땀을 쥐게 하는 + noun · 손에 땀을 쥐고 봤어요
손에 땀을 쥐다.m: to be on the edge of one's seat; to be tense with suspense
손에 땀을 쥐다.ex: 마지막까지 손에 땀을 쥐게 하는 경기였어요.
손에 땀을 쥐다.x: It was a nail-biting game right up to the end.
손에 땀을 쥐다.e: Literally 'to grip sweat in one's hands' — sweaty palms from tension.
손에 땀을 쥐다.t: Most often a modifier: 손에 땀을 쥐게 하는 경기/장면.

묘안.ex: 아무리 생각해도 좋은 묘안이 떠오르지 않아요.
묘안.x: No matter how much I think, no clever idea comes to mind.

신자.ex: 그 성당에는 매주 많은 신자들이 모입니다.
신자.x: Many believers gather at that cathedral every week.
신자.e: Literally 'believing person'. -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

절수.x: Because the drought was severe, citizens were urged to save water.
절수.e: Literally 'saving water', using water in moderation.
절수.t: Pronounced [절쑤]; 절수형 means 'water-saving', as in 절수형 변기.

두드러기.ex: 새우를 먹고 나서 온몸에 두드러기가 났어요.
두드러기.x: After eating shrimp, I broke out in hives all over my body.
두드러기.e: Native word; probably linked to 두드러지다 'to stick out', describing the raised bumps.
두드러기.t: Use 두드러기가 나다 'to break out in hives'.

시행령.ex: 정부는 새 법의 시행령을 다음 달에 발표할 예정입니다.
시행령.x: The government plans to announce the enforcement decree for the new law next month.
시행령.e: Literally 'implementation order' — a presidential decree that fills in a law's details.
시행령.t: Pronounced [시행녕] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

변조.m: alteration, tampering (of a genuine document); (tech) modulation
변조.ex: 그는 신분증의 생년월일을 변조한 혐의를 받았어요.
변조.x: He was accused of altering the date of birth on his ID card.
변조.t: 위조 is faking a document from scratch; 변조 is tampering with a real one.

가결.m: approval (of a bill or motion), passage
가결.x: Whether the motion passes will be decided tomorrow.
가결.t: Bills and motions are 가결되다 (passed) or 부결되다 (voted down).

매표.ex: 선거 전에 현금을 나눠 주는 것은 매표 행위입니다.
매표.x: Handing out cash before an election is an act of vote buying.
매표.e: Literally 'buying ballots'; a homonym of 매표 'ticket selling', as in 매표소.
매표.t: Politicians often attack rivals' cash handouts as 매표용 포퓰리즘, 'vote-buying populism'.

화해무드.ex: 정상회담 이후 두 나라 사이에 화해무드가 조성됐어요.
화해무드.x: After the summit, a mood of reconciliation formed between the two countries.
화해무드.e: 화해 'reconciliation' plus English 'mood'; Konglish 무드 means 'atmosphere'.

불가지론.ex: 그는 신의 존재에 대해 불가지론의 입장을 취해요.
불가지론.x: He takes an agnostic position on the existence of God.
불가지론.e: Literally 'cannot-know theory', a neat match for Greek 'a-gnostic'.
불가지론.t: Add -자 for the person: 불가지론자 is an agnostic, 무신론자 an atheist.

문단.ex: 그 소설가는 스무 살에 문단의 주목을 받았어요.
문단.x: That novelist caught the attention of the literary world at twenty.
문단.t: Don't confuse it with the homonym 문단 'paragraph'; 문단에 나오다 clearly means the literary world.

과장법.x: 'I waited till my eyes fell out' is an expression using hyperbole.
과장법.e: Literally 'boast-stretch method' — saying more than is true for effect.

선사시대.ex: 선사시대에는 문자가 없어서 기록이 남아 있지 않아요.
선사시대.x: There was no writing in prehistoric times, so no records remain.
선사시대.e: Literally 'the era before history' — before written records.

재고하다.x: That plan needs to be reconsidered.
재고하다.t: Homonym: 재고 (在庫) means stock or inventory, and 제고 means to raise.

구애되다.m: to be bound by, to be constrained by
구애되다.ex: 나이에 구애되지 않고 누구나 지원할 수 있습니다.
구애되다.x: Anyone can apply regardless of age.
구애되다.t: Almost always negative: -에 구애되지 않고 'regardless of'; unrelated to 구애 'courtship'.

무마하다.m: to hush up, to smooth over, to appease
무마하다.x: The company tried to hush up the incident with money.
무마하다.e: Literally 'stroke and rub' — soothing a problem until it quiets down.
무마하다.t: Usually has a negative ring: 사건을 무마하다 'to hush up an incident'.

하회하다.m: to fall below, to be lower than (a figure)
하회하다.ex: 이번 분기 실적이 시장 기대치를 하회했습니다.
하회하다.x: This quarter's earnings fell short of market expectations.
하회하다.e: Literally 'go around below' — running under a mark.
하회하다.t: The native equivalent 밑돌다 is more common in everyday news.

졸렬하다.ex: 상대의 약점을 이용하는 것은 졸렬한 방법이에요.
졸렬하다.x: Exploiting your opponent's weakness is a petty tactic.

베이비붐세대.x: As the baby boomers retire, the workforce is shrinking.
베이비붐세대.e: From English 'baby boom' plus 세대 'generation'; in Korea, people born roughly 1955–1963.

홀연.m: suddenly, all of a sudden, unexpectedly
홀연.ex: 그는 어느 날 홀연 자취를 감췄어요.
홀연.x: One day he suddenly vanished without a trace.
홀연.e: Literally 'in a sudden manner'; a literary word from stories and essays.
홀연.t: Literary; in everyday speech say 갑자기 instead.

기저.ex: 이 정책의 기저에는 평등이라는 가치가 깔려 있습니다.
기저.x: Underlying this policy is the value of equality.
기저.t: Typical pattern: ~의 기저에는 ~이/가 깔려 있다 'underlying ~ is ~'.
